judge: claude -p --model opus, sealed, Read only, stream-json transcript (page.jpg opened checked); route-judge judgePrompt translation form, image + stored OCR; blind (no arm in the prompt)

per_page.title: [Historiae tres de S. Anna, de S. Joachim et de S. Joseph]

a.reader_note: The translation is complete and accurate overall. One clause about Joachim's double gifts is misconstrued: the fields and wool become the place where people labour, when they are what he gave.

r.reader_note: A mostly fluent and complete translation, but the opening misreads 'indigne' as 'needy' and makes the honoured parents the devotee's own instead of Mary's, which skews the argument.

per_page.title: Bibliotheca Hispana vetus, sive Hispanorum, qui usquam unquamve scripto aliquid

a.reader_note: A reader would find that the list of 'four kings' names only three, with John I missing, and that Livy is wrongly placed among the sacred writers while St Gregory is left out.

r.reader_note: A reader would get the wrong list of the four kings, Livy wrongly called a sacred writer with St Gregory missing, 'dear to few' instead of 'dear as few were', and the loan of the codex running the wrong way. These errors come from following a garbled transcription instead of the page image.

per_page.title: Artis Auriferae quam Chemiam vocant, volumen primum

a.reader_note: This is a faithful, complete rendering of the Sun–Moon epistle passage. The only gap is the opening seam, where the adjective split across from the previous page (-tilem) isn't translated.

r.reader_note: The page is translated in full and reads faithfully. Two small slips: the Moon's role as subject in the epistle clause is blurred, and 'vacare' is given as 'be free' instead of 'devote ourselves to'.

per_page.title: Joh. Joach. Becheri ... Opvscvla Chymica Rariora

a.reader_note: A faithful, complete rendering of Becher's account of the delayed privilege, the Mecklenburg journey and his own expenses. One clause is wrongly made conditional ('if' should be 'for'), and the gloss calls the privilege 'royal', which the page doesn't say.

r.reader_note: This is a faithful, complete rendering of the author's complaint that the privilege was held up during the Hague peace talks and that he paid for a year in Amsterdam out of his own pocket. The only roughness is at the opening seam, where the carried-over words 'had expected' are lost.

per_page.title: Opera Poetica omnia. 4

a.reader_note: Mostly a sound verse translation, but the opening 'just as' simile is gone and the last line ends in an invented 'into the arms' where the page has 'instar' ('like').

r.reader_note: This is the right page and it is complete, but the opening simile and the Bacchic cry are misconstrued, 'ador' and 'cortina' are mistranslated, and the note on Cirrha is wrong.

per_page.title: Antiquitates Graecae et Romanae. [1]

a.reader_note: The plate's number, Tab. CXXXXII, is missing, and a faint passage showing through from another leaf is translated as if it were a margin note on this plate.

r.reader_note: This is a plate (Tab. CXXXXII) of five engravings. The translation leaves out the plate number and presents bleed-through text from another page as a margin note on this one.

per_page.title: Commentariorvm Alchymiae Andreae Libavii Med. D. Pars .... 2, Continens Tractatv

a.reader_note: Most of the page reads well. However, a garbled margin note leaks 'natron according to Agricola' into the arthritis list, Stabiae becomes a 'wasting hospital', and Fabaria is placed in France.

r.reader_note: The marginal note is mistranslated, and its 'Agricola' has been copied into the main text. Several names and qualities are misread: Sinuessa appears as 'Siefana', and the 'golden' waters of Pfäfers become 'dark'.

per_page.title: Musicae practicae elementa in usum scholae Magdeburgensis edita, a M. Gallo dres

r.reader_note: Both rules (IIII on rests, V on three adjacent figures) are translated accurately. The staff descriptions are loose and the catchword 'Exem' is missing, but neither changes the meaning.

per_page.title: Architectonice Musices Universalis, Ex qua Melopoeam Per Universa Et Solida Fund

a.reader_note: This is a faithful, complete translation of the end of the mode descriptions and the start of Chapter XXI on counterpoint. The Greek πλάγιος appears only in transliteration, and the sentence saying what 'counterpoint' means today is slightly ambiguous.

r.reader_note: This is a faithful translation of p. 56 (tones V–XII, plagal and authentic modes, and the start of Ch. XXI on counterpoint). It leaves out that the authentic tones are the 'odd' ones, and it supplies a verb the page doesn't have in the sentence cut off at the end of the page.

per_page.title: Singularium Andreae Libavii Pars .... 2, Multa Scitu Iucunda, Ac necessaria cont

a.reader_note: The translation reads accurately overall, but the phrase 'univocally in the feminine manner' does not make sense. The page says 'by seed' (seminio), which the transcription misread.

r.reader_note: The page and the date 1599 at Rothenburg on the Tauber are right, but the translation says the author will decide the question when the Latin leaves it to each reader. It also turns 'by seed' into 'by the feminine' and adds a note explaining it.

per_page.title: Confessio catholica. 2,2

a.reader_note: Readers would see a marginal note that isn't on the page, while the main text loses who approves the reasoning. The last line also finishes a sentence that the page leaves cut off.

r.reader_note: The body translation is accurate and complete. But it shows a marginal note that isn't on the page, and the last sentence is finished with invented wording ('purpose perpetually') where the page breaks off mid-word.

per_page.title: Singularium Andreae Libavii pars .... 3, Continens octo libros bituminum et affi

a.reader_note: The body text is a faithful, complete translation, but the last margin note calls Nicander and Cardano's dispute an 'agreement', which contradicts the text beside it.

r.reader_note: The reader is told that the Scottish coal fires burn without harming the inhabitants, but the page says the opposite. The margin note is turned into the author agreeing with Nicander and Cardanus, when it actually marks a dispute between them.

per_page.title: Breviarium monasticum Pauli V. pont. max. jussu editum, pro omnibus sub regula S

a.reader_note: This is a faithful and complete rendering of the end of the psalm, the antiphon, versicles, the red rubric on lessons and 1 Cor 4:1-7. The only additions are the completed blessing formulas, which the page gives only as opening words.

r.reader_note: A faithful, complete rendering of the end of the psalm, the versicles, the red rubric on when the Common's lessons are read, and 1 Cor 4:1-7 in Douay-like English. It breaks off correctly at the catchword 'ac-'. Only small wording slips in the rubric.

per_page.title: Historiae Augustae tomus V. Ab imperio Caroli Magni, ad Fridericum primum, cogno

a.reader_note: The sentence about Zengi besieging Edessa is missing and patched with a guessed 'attacked'. Conrad's courteous reception of Cardinal Guido is merged into the privilege grant, and the marginal note's 'like cattle to the slaughter' is lost.

r.reader_note: Readers would be told that Sanguinus was an Armenian citizen living in a tower at Edessa. The page actually says he was the Saracen prince who besieged the city, and it was a separate Armenian who held the tower. The left margin note and the last word on the page are also garbled.

per_page.title: Opus aureum. Musice castigatissimu. De Gregoriana.et figuratiua atque contrapuct

a.reader_note: The verse and prose are roughly right, but the table and the closing rule give the wrong finals: F-fa-ut appears where the page has C-fa-ut, the rule numbers and rows are shifted, and mode 1 is said to end on mi.

r.reader_note: The modal-finals table and the commentary contain wrong note names ('L-fa-ut' for C-fa-ut, 'neutral' for deuterus), a misnumbered rule (3rd instead of 1st), and one cell rendered as nonsense, so the page's music theory comes out partly wrong.

per_page.title: Musicae, id est, artis canendi libri duo. Autor sebaldus heyden.

a.reader_note: The translation is faithful and complete. It covers the page's statements, the fractions 2/1, 4/2, 6/3 and 12/6, and the signs Φ, ¢, O2, C2 and Ɔ, all of which match the scan, though one phrase is worded loosely.

r.reader_note: The translation reads faithfully except that the definition of 'Duple' is reversed: the page says it makes two notes worth one, but the translation says it makes one worth two.

per_page.title: Istoria De' Poeti Greci Et Di Que' Che'n Greca Lingua han poetato

a.reader_note: This is a faithful translation of the end of the Thespis entry, the Teucer note and the start of the Tiberius sketch. Only the opening run-on Latin quotation muddles who used the cart and added the actor.

r.reader_note: A faithful, complete translation of the Thespis, Teucer and Tiberius entries. There are a few small slips: 'plures, certioresque' becomes 'more and more certain', 'Sassi solamente' becomes 'Know only', and it is unclear who contradicts Tiberius's opinion.

per_page.title: L. Annaei Senecae epistolae CXXIII. M. Antonii Mureti notis et emendationibus il

a.reader_note: The translation is faithful and complete, and all the declaimers' names in the margins are kept. One line follows a transcription misreading: the speaker's own 'What shall I say?' is given as a question put to him, and there are a few small slips in person and wording.

r.reader_note: This is the right page and the whole page is there. But several sentences are mistranslated or garbled: the 'facinus indignum commissum' line, a reversed 'you/I do not fear' line, and a lament attributed to the opponent. The Latin is only partly reliable as a guide here.

per_page.title: Confessio fidei exhibita ... in Comitiis Augustae anno 1530

a.reader_note: A faithful, complete rendering of the Apology's argument against 'fides formata', but the first line comes from a split-word fragment (misread as "Et non") and reads as a self-contained question instead of the end of the previous page's sentence.

r.reader_note: This is a faithful translation of the page. The only odd spot is the first sentence, 'And to one not noticing these voices?', which is really the end of a sentence carried over from the previous page.

per_page.title: Commentarii in Evangelium D. nostri Jesu Christi secundum Joannem, facili et per

a.reader_note: A faithful, readable rendering of the page. Two small things are lost: the servant is no longer called a 'flatterer', and the explicit 'he did none of these things' is missing.

r.reader_note: The translation is fluent and mostly faithful, but it leaves out who is being refuted (the flatterer) and wrongly suggests that Christ was struck a second time.

per_page.title: Mirabilia Fidei Divinae, Quae Deus Velut Tot Miracula In Quolibet Christiano, Qu

a.reader_note: The page lists the reader's faults, but one is turned around: the original says the reader believes with too little simplicity, while the English says they believe 'far too simply'.

r.reader_note: A faithful and complete rendering of the list of faults against faith, but the cross-reference to no. 246 is missing, so that clause looks like it points only to no. 258.

per_page.title: Artis musicae, methodice legibus logicis informatae libri duo. Ad totum musices

a.reader_note: This is a faithful translation of the page. The list of five pieces is correct: Herpold for 5 voices, Utendal for 6, Herpold for 5, Utendal for 4, Herpold for 5. So is the remark that Clemens's 'Qui consolabatur me' is assigned here by some but seems to the author more Ionian than Lydian. Both range-and-mediation headings and the canons at the unison for 4 and 3 voices are kept, and nothing is dropped or added.

r.reader_note: The text, the incipits, the names and all the numbers (5, 6, 5, 4, 5; Fuga 4 and 3) are rendered faithfully; only the first music staff placeholder is missing, and the editorial note on 'Coniuncti' is loose.

per_page.title: Tu en hagiois patros hēmōn Dionysiu tu Areiopagitu ta sōzomena panta. 2, Tomus S

a.reader_note: Readers would be told Dionysius quotes others, when the page says Isaac quotes Dionysius, which is the point being argued. The epithet 'the Syrian' is missing, and the page's misprinted date 338 has been silently changed to 378 in the text.

r.reader_note: The Cabassut quotation is reversed: it says the Areopagite cites Isaac's books on the Angels, when the page says Isaac cites the Areopagite. It also loses 'the Syrian' from Isaac's name. The rest, including the page's own date of 338 for Ephrem's death and the notes, is rendered faithfully.

per_page.title: Polygraphia sacra : seu elucidarium Biblicum historico-mysticum, in quo omnes et

a.reader_note: In the Acts section, the material on Paul's Areopagus speech ('Unknown God'), his defence before Felix and the storm at sea is missing or run together, and the margin note markers there are wrong.

r.reader_note: A reader would find a large passage on Paul missing (the Areopagus, Felix and the resurrection quote). Several margin notes are garbled or duplicated, and saints are rendered as 'the Lord'.

per_page.title: Quod Karolus IV. Augustus, non dissipaverit Imperii Patrimonium, quatenus pertin

a.reader_note: The translation follows the Latin closely and is complete. Only the editorial notes and summary have small slips: a wrong death date for Rettenpacher and an author name the page does not support.

r.reader_note: A faithful, complete translation of Charles IV and the Kingdom of Arles. It has a few loose phrases, and the summary says the claim rests on the Westphalia and Nijmegen treaties, when the page says it was not given up in them.

per_page.title: Commentarii in Evangelium D. Nostri Jesu Christi secundum Lucam, facili et persp

a.reader_note: Most of the page reads well, but the Greek grammar point at the end is garbled. The page says αὐτὸς refers back to οἶκος ('house'), which is masculine in Greek, but the translation has it referring to 'son', so the argument no longer makes sense.

r.reader_note: The Greek grammar note is garbled: the page says αὐτός refers back to οἶκος (house), but the translation says 'son', so the commentator's point about gender is lost.

per_page.title: D. Augustini De musica libri VI

a.reader_note: Several of the musical intervals and numbers are wrong: the twelfth should be the eleventh, the octave should be the tone, 'tone' is missing from the refuted claim, '81' is dropped, and a phantom '11' appears. A reader would learn the wrong music theory from this page.

r.reader_note: I'd reject this translation. It follows a faulty transcription: the page joins a 9:8 tone to a 3:2 fifth over the terms 27, 18, 16, but the reader is told 4:3 and 12, 9, 8, and later passages are garbled, including the numbers 24.2 and 16.2 and a dropped 81.

per_page.title: Oratio de divina origine, atque utIlitate Multiplici praestantissimae ac nobilis

a.reader_note: A faithful, complete translation of the discourse on music's inventors; only the guessed sense of the opening fragment 'cere' and the lost 'TVBAL' catchword stand out.

r.reader_note: This is a faithful, complete translation of the page: the conflicting accounts of who invented music (Tubal, Orpheus, Amphion), the references to Polydore Vergil (book 1, chapter 14) and Quintilian (book 1, chapter 16), and the argument that people cannot have lived without music from Adam to Tubal. The only small issues are that the Greek word μοῦσα becomes plain 'Muse' and the catchword TVBAL is left out, as is usual.

per_page.title: Discursus Iuris Publici, De Augustissimae Domus Austriacae Iuribus Ac Praeeminen

a.reader_note: The translation is mostly faithful, but its last sentence adds a prayer to 'God the Best and Greatest' that is not on the page, it misreads the Turkish war as 'only fierce war', and it gives Heuterus the wrong name.

r.reader_note: Two key statements are reversed: the Austrians are said to have sought a European monarchy, and our own arms are said to have been broken by the Turks. The claim that no emperor was a tyrant also loses its limit to the Austrian emperors.

per_page.title: Enchiridion musices

a.reader_note: A faithful, complete rendering of the counterpoint rules. The only gap is a possible 'fifth' left out of the seventh rule's list of intervals.

per_page.title: Deutsches theatrum chemicum, auf welchem der berühmtesten Philosophen und Alchym

a.reader_note: A faithful, complete rendering of the Geber, Arnold and Bernhardus citations; the only rough spots are how 'Cap. 4. 1. Rosar.' is read and the guessed ending of the last word, which continues on the next page.

r.reader_note: This is a faithful, complete rendering of the page's Geber, Arnoldus and Bernhardus citations, with the chapter and book numbers correct. Only the split word at the end of the page is guessed rather than marked.

per_page.title: Die teuflische Magie existirt nicht : die Antwort des Landpfarrers an den Herr

a.reader_note: A close, complete translation of the page. The addressee 'H. Weltmann' appears in English as 'Mr. Worldly Man', which reads as an epithet rather than the name; the Apelles note is accurate.

r.reader_note: Reads faithfully overall: all three 'Wenn' paragraphs, Weltmann and both 'Cobbler, stick to your last' lines are there, but 'einreden' (to meddle) is twice rendered as 'talk out of', and the second time 'their duties' is added.

per_page.title: Die ältere Geschichte des Gerichtes Asch, dessen ursprünglicher Reichs-Unmitte

a.reader_note: A complete and accurate translation. The family name is made uniform as 'Neuburg' although the page spells it Neydberg, Neuburg and Neuberg, and the 'Virtus majestatica' gloss wrongly adds 'imperial'.

r.reader_note: A complete, faithful rendering of the Neuberg fief argument and the 14 Bohemian objections; only 'pretend' for 'prätendiren' (claim) and a singular holder turned plural would trip a careful reader.

per_page.title: Christliche Leich-predigt von rechter Sterb-kunst : gehalten in Mülhausen den 11

a.reader_note: This is a faithful, complete translation of the page. All six reasons for comfort (men's wrath, bodily tribulation, loss of goods, sadness, tears, death) are kept, and every marginal Bible reference (Ps. 103:11, 17 through ibid. 5:24) matches the image. The heading for section 2 and its seam word 'When' are kept too.

r.reader_note: This is a complete and faithful translation of page 13. The image confirms the transcription, all eight marginal scripture references (Ps. 103:11, 17 through ibid. 5:24) are correct and placed against the right lines, and the page ends on the same unfinished section heading "2. … When" as the original.

per_page.title: Das freudige Danck-Opfer Treuer Unterthanen wurde Wegen Höchstbeglückter Zurüc

a.reader_note: The translation is complete and accurate overall, but two Bible quotations use King James wording instead of this page's text, and one of them drops the darkness image the passage is about.

r.reader_note: The translation is complete and accurate except at Job 6:4, where it gives the King James 'poison … drinketh up' instead of the page's 'their wrath consumes my spirit'.

per_page.title: Tabelle über die Menge der auflöslichen Bestandtheile welche aus den Gewächsen d

a.reader_note: The translated plant names and habitats are mostly sound, but many extract fractions are wrong, missing or in the wrong column, rows are shifted, and the notes attribute the sigla to authors on no evidence from the page.

r.reader_note: The names, places and flowering times are translated correctly, but many of the extract fractions in the last two columns are wrong, dropped or in the wrong cell, so the numbers can't be trusted.

per_page.title: Kurtzer Discurs, Darinnen die Natur, Lauff un[d] Bedröwung des Cometen, so Anno

a.reader_note: The German prose is translated accurately, but Haly's Latin is left untranslated in a note, so the reader misses its main point (morning means the effect comes soon, evening means it comes late). The woodcut description also mentions one comet where the image shows three.

r.reader_note: The text matches the page and ends mid-sentence at 'gesehen' as the page does. 'Affliction' is a loose rendering of 'bedröwung', which means the comet's threat, and the image note undercounts the comets.

per_page.title: Die Landwirthschaft des Königreichs Böhmen / 4,4 : ... von den Steinkohlen und

a.reader_note: The translation is faithful and complete. All three numbered paragraphs on bituminous woods are fully rendered, with nothing dropped or changed. The added note glossing Teplitz as Teplice in Bohemia is accurate.

r.reader_note: This is a faithful, complete translation of §5 on bituminous woods. It covers all three numbered points, Teplitz, and jet, and adds or drops nothing.

per_page.title: Erkenntnis und Irrtum: Skizzen zur Psychologie der Forschung

a.reader_note: A faithful, complete translation. The names, dates (1615, 1634, 1824), the threefold area ratio, the footnote and the reasoning about A, B and C all match the page.

r.reader_note: A complete and faithful translation: the Archimedes example, the dates for Mersenne (1615) and Roberval (1634), Galileo's threefold area and the footnote all match the page.

per_page.title: Psychologie und Erkenntnistheorie

a.reader_note: A faithful, complete translation of the page. The only loss is the original's letter-spaced emphasis on 'processes', 'matter' and 'its own inner nature'.

r.reader_note: This is a faithful, complete translation of p. 494 on natural necessity, Kant versus Hume, and where the concept of necessity comes from; only the original's spaced-type emphasis is missing.

per_page.title: Vom Cometen Anno 1596. Jm anfang des Monats Julij erschienen

a.reader_note: A faithful, complete translation of the comet passage: comets come from the macrocosm's imagination, compared to birthmarks caused by a pregnant woman's cravings. It ends mid-sentence at "which", as the page does.

r.reader_note: A faithful, complete rendering of the comet-and-imagination passage. The Latin terms are kept and glossed accurately, and it breaks off at 'which' just as the page does, so it isn't truncated.

per_page.title: Bileams Abfertigung, oder Gründliche Wiederlegung der Astrologie und aller anver

a.reader_note: Most of the page reads faithfully, but the key conclusion is reversed: the author says Scripture supports only the smallest part of astrology, and the translation says 'not the least part'. The last line also adds words that are not on the page.

r.reader_note: The page translation is accurate overall until its final line. There it adds 'to prefigure the life and condition', which this page does not contain, and it renders 'zukunft Christi' as 'the future of Christ' instead of 'the coming of Christ'.

per_page.title: Compendium Chymico-Philosophicum. Das ist: Chymischer Kern und Außzug der allerf

a.reader_note: The translation is faithful and complete. The fire symbol △ is explained correctly in a note, and the running head 'Of the Secret of the World' appears as if it opened the paragraph.

r.reader_note: This is a faithful and complete translation of the page, including the running head, the fire symbol (△) with a correct gloss and the catchword 'Without'. A few phrases are very literal; for example, 'I consider no chatterer' reads a little stiffly but keeps the sense.

per_page.title: Rath in pestilentz zeiten wie man die verhueten und in nothfall curiren sol zu n

a.reader_note: This is a faithful, complete rendering of the page's plague precautions (third to seventh) and the start of the personal preservatives section, with all lists, times and the wagon-track distance kept.

r.reader_note: Mostly faithful translation of the plague-prevention rules. The sixth rule is mistranslated (it should say to appoint as few attendants as possible), and the fifth rule loses the word 'wares'.

per_page.title: Schreiben eines Holländischen Volontairs bey der Königlich-Preußischen Armee in

a.reader_note: This is a faithful, complete translation of the page. All times (10, half past 1, 3, half past 5, 6), the three assaults, the units, the places and Prince Ferdinand's graze match the image, and it ends correctly mid-sentence at 'The Saxon Prince' before the catchword 'Xaver'.

r.reader_note: This is a complete and accurate account of the sortie from Prague; the reader may be puzzled by 'the small side' (Prague's Lesser Town) and by the attack that 'passed' the front, which on the page enveloped it.

per_page.title: Radius Mathematicus, Oder Erklärunge und Gebrauch deß Mathematischen Marchiersta

a.reader_note: The page reads as a faithful, complete translation of the two-station height method and its use for width; the only rough spot is the sentence that breaks off at the foot of the page.

r.reader_note: The translation is faithful and complete down to the catchword 'gemesse-'; only one clause about retrying 'as at the first station' is slightly misrendered.

per_page.title: Observatio und bedeutunge des cometen so dieses M.D.LVI. jhar im anfange des Mer

a.reader_note: The translation matches the page closely, including the 11, 15 and 6 degree readings and the times of 12:30 and 2 o'clock; only the continuity note is wrong, since 'four degrees' is the catchword leading onto the next page.

r.reader_note: The fourth-day meridian transit is put at two o'clock when the page says one o'clock, so the observation time is wrong. The rest of the page is complete and accurate.

per_page.title: Einweihungs-Predigt, an dem ... Tage der feyerl. Einweihung des neuerbauten Gott

a.reader_note: The sermon text and footnote are translated faithfully, but the quoted prayer of Solomon (1 Kings 8:28–30) has been partly replaced with King James wording: 'praise' becomes 'cry' and 'be gracious' becomes 'forgive'.

r.reader_note: This is a faithful, complete rendering of the sermon page, including Solomon's prayer, Isaiah 2:3 / Ps. 5:8 and the footnote about the house of prayer standing on a hill; only small tagging and wording nuances differ.

per_page.title: Königlich-Spannisches Manifest, Enthaltend Deß Königs in Spanien Prætension, So

a.reader_note: The translation is faithful and complete. The only slip is in the last two words: 'and as' should be 'and there', because the page ends with 'all-' and the catchword 'da' completes it as 'allda'.

r.reader_note: A faithful, complete rendering with all names and dates (1708, 1732, 1313, 1318, 1530) intact; only the last word misreads the split word 'all-/da' as 'as', and 'granted' softens the 1732 guarantee.

per_page.title: Sendschreiben von dem Vielfraß ... welcher aus Böhmen bürtig und sich eine Zeit

a.reader_note: A faithful rendering of the 1702 title page (author, Tannstädt, the Bohemian glutton in Leipzig and Berlin, Käyser in Mühlhausen); only the summary's 'notorious' and some awkward closing syntax stand out.

r.reader_note: This is a faithful title-page translation: names, places, bookseller and the year 1702 are all correct. The phrasing is a little awkward ('Open Letter', 'spent some time ... staying').

per_page.title: Eine Merckwürdige und Verwunderungs-wehrte Offenbahrung: Betreffend I. Die Rebel

a.reader_note: A faithful, complete translation that checks against the image: Gen. 18:17, the forty years, 1601, Dublin, Ezekiel 4:6 and the man's dislike of enthusiasts' visions are all right, and the split word 'Unge-' is sensibly rendered as 'ini-' (iniquity).

r.reader_note: A faithful, complete translation of the page; the numbers, names and references (Gen. XVIII.17, 40 years, 1601, Ezech. IV.6, Dublin) are correct, and it ends on the 'un-' word break that continues on the next page.

per_page.title: Beyträge zur Wassergeschichte von Böhmen / 1

a.reader_note: A faithful, complete translation of p. 97: the sulphur-rich iron ochre of the Bechin water, its red tincture and Balsamum Martis, the magnet attracting the iron only after calcination, and the near-absence of salts, alum, saltpetre and vitriol. Only 'iron mountain-yellow' reads awkwardly.

r.reader_note: The translation is complete and faithful to the page, which the transcription matches. The last sentence is unclear: it does not show that the author rejects other writers' claims that the earth contains alum, saltpeter or vitriol salt.

per_page.title: Theatrum Machinarum Generale: Schau-Platz der Mechanischen Wissenschafften

a.reader_note: All the engraved captions are translated correctly. The only real error is in the figure description: Fig. IV is called water-powered, but the plate clearly shows horses driving the mill.

r.reader_note: All the engraved captions are translated correctly. The only problems are in the editorial description and summary: they call the horse-driven mud mill water-powered and say Sturm made the improvements.

per_page.title: Die Anfänge der Musik

a.reader_note: A reader would get the wrong alternative metre (3/8 instead of 3/2), would read 'quarter tones' where the page means quarter notes, and would see the unfinished last sentence given an object ('something exotic') that the page doesn't have.

r.reader_note: The second time signature is wrong (the page says 6/4 and 3/2, not 3/8), and the last sentence finishes with an invented object, 'something exotic', even though the German breaks off unfinished at the page end.

per_page.title: Der Auffrichtige Unverfälschte Engelländische Wahrsager, Das ist: Ein Prognostic
